summary_paragraph: A woman with complex bariatric surgical history (prior Roux-en-Y gastric bypass with later open reversal), chronic abdominal pain, and anxiety/depression presented with acute worsening nausea, vomiting, and frequent watery diarrhea. Initial evaluation showed stable vital signs, no leukocytosis, and metabolic acidosis consistent with dehydration; stool testing returned positive for toxigenic Clostridium difficile, consistent with a second recurrence. She was treated with IV fluids, antiemetics, and started on an oral vancomycin taper/pulse regimen; symptoms improved with return of oral tolerance and abdominal pain back toward baseline. Chronic conditions (seizure disorder, depression/anxiety, insomnia, and nutritional supplementation) were continued, bowel regimen laxatives were held due to diarrhea, and she was discharged home with instructions to complete the vancomycin taper and follow up with primary care and gastroenterology (including discussion of colonoscopy repeat given prior poor prep and consideration of other causes of chronic diarrhea, and reassessment of ongoing PPI use in the setting of recurrent C. difficile).
problems: Major depressive disorder, single episode, unspecified
Epilepsy, unspecified, not intractable, without status epilepticus
